layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Anything Model (SAM), have revealed robust generaliza-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion capabilities. However, applying these models directly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to medical image segmentation still exposes perfor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mance degradation. In this paper, we propose a learnable

layout_dets.text: co-teaching paradigm, resulting in more robust outcomes.

layout_dets.text: Knowledge Distillation (SKD) to transfer useful knowledge

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from SAM to two sub-networks, enabling them to learn

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Despite the progress that has been achieved, these methods still

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: face numerous challenges, particularly in further enhancing the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model's generalization capability.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Recently, foundational models like the Segment Anything

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Model (SAM) [17] have demonstrated promising progress

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in segmentation tasks. However, SAM cannot be directly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: applied to all segmentation scenarios, especially in medical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image segmentation tasks [18]. To address this issue, several

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: studies [18], [19], [20], [21] integrate an adapter into SAM

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and subsequently fine-tune SAM on the specific dataset for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: downstream tasks. Furthermore, some studies [22], [23] have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: incorporated SAM to enhance the accuracy of pseudo-labels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for unlabeled data, thereby improving model performance.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: These methods supply SAM with precise prediction points

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or boxes as prompts to generate pseudo-labels. However,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a limitation of this strategy is that providing incorrect prompts

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can directly lead to a substantial decrease in SAM's effec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tiveness. While numerous studies have integrated SAM into

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: medical segmentation tasks, the optimal utilization of SAM's

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: generalization capability to enhance semi-supervised medical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image segmentation remains an area deserving of further

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: investigation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To this end, as depicted in Fig. 1(d), we propose a learnable

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: prompting SAM-induced knowledge distillation framework

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (termed KnowSAM) for semi-supervised medical image seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation. KnowSAM leverages the generalization ability

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of SAM through distillation learning to enhance segmen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation performance. Specifically, we propose a Multi-view

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Co-training (MC) strategy, where two subnets engage in a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: co-teaching paradigm and mutually correct each other. Addi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tionally, the MC incorporates a Hybrid Aggregation Module

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (HAM) to adaptively merge prediction maps with entropy

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: maps and dissimilarity maps, reducing discordant predic-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions and uncertainties between the two subnets. Furthermore,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we propose a Learnable Prompt Strategy (LPS) to extract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dense prompts from a designed lightweight network and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: integrate them into SAM's decoder. Concurrently, we intro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: duce an adapter module in SAM's image encoder and decoder

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: layers for fine-tuning, enhancing SAM's performance on med-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ical segmentation tasks. Additionally, we present a simple

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: yet effective Uncertainty-Guided Data Augmentation (UGDA)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: method to boost the generalization of our model by increasing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: diversity in unlabeled data. Lastly, we present a SAM-induced

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Knowledge Distillation (SKD) strategy to enable the two

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sub-networks to learn valuable information from SAM.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Our main contributions are summarized as follows:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • We propose a novel KnowSAM framework to harness

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the generalization capabilities of the foundation model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: through distillation learning to improve semi-supervised

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: medical image segmentation performance. Importantly,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: our SAM distillation framework can be seamlessly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: applied to other semi-supervised segmentation methods.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • We present a multi-view co-training component to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: integrate multi-view maps, including the subnets’ out-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: puts, entropy uncertainty maps, and spatial information

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from regions where discrepancies exist in the subnets'

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: predictions. This approach gradually reduces cognitive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: differences between the two subnets, leading to improved

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation accuracy.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • A learnable prompt strategy is proposed to dynamically

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: provide effective feature prompts. This strategy prevents

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performance degradation of SAM caused by incorrect

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hard coordinates, thus improving SAM's capability in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: medical segmentation tasks.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Extensive experimental results on a diversity of medical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation tasks demonstrate that our model outper-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: forms the other state-of-the-art semi-supervised methods.

layout_dets.text: II. RELATED WORK

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A. Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Pseudo-labeling, consistency regularization, and co-training

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are three common methods in semi-supervised medical image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation, and we discuss these related studies below.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1) Pseudo-Labeling: Pseudo-labeling methods involve gen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: erating pseudo-annotations for unlabeled data and then

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: using them as labels for model retraining. For example,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Zeng et al. [24] designed a novel double-threshold pseudo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: labeling method for dual-task image segmentation and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: classification to enhance the joint model's utilization of unla-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: beled data. Yao et al. [25] proposed a confidence-aware cross

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pseudo-supervision algorithm, which enhances the quality of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pseudo labels for unlabeled images by utilizing Fourier trans-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: formations. Moreover, strategies such as uncertainty guidance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and confidence awareness can improve the quality of generated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pseudo-labels, with higher confidence typically leading to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: more effective pseudo-labels [26], [27].

layout_dets.text: counterparts for consistency regularization, enhancing the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model's generalization by extracting valuable information

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: B. Knowledge Distillation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: KD technology has achieved significant results in model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: compression and transfer learning, yet there has been rela-

layout_dets.text: tively less exploration in the SSL domain. KD guides the

layout_dets.text: image segmentation by providing more informative training

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: framework that improves voxel representation learning and

layout_dets.text: structural distillation of pair-wise similarities. To tackle the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: an anatomical-aware contrastive distillation framework for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: semi-supervised medical image segmentation, which leverages

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: iterative contrastive distillation, soft negative labeling, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: anatomical contrast sampling to boost segmentation accuracy.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Additionally, Shu et al. [37] employed a cross-mix teaching

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: paradigm and a lightweight transductive monitor for active

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: knowledge extraction. This serves as a bridge between the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: teacher and student models, improving performance in sce-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: narios with limited supervision.

layout_dets.text: IV. EXPERIMENTS AND RESULTS

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A. Datasets

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1) Colonoscopy Datasets: Five colonoscopy datasets are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: used for polyp segmentation, including ETIS [47], CVC-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ClinicDB [48], CVC-ColonDB [49], CVC-300 [50], and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Kvasir [51]. Following the previous setting [52], a total

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of 1, 450 images are selected from the CVC-ClinicDB and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Kvasir datasets to form the training set, while all remaining

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 798 images are used for testing.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2) Ultrasound Thyroid Nodule Datasets: Three ultrasound

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: datasets are used, namely TN3K [53], TG3K [54], and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: DDTI [55]. The TN3K dataset consists of 3, 493 ultrasound

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images, with 2, 879 images for training and 614 ones for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: testing. The DDTI dataset contains 637 ultrasound images

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: captured using the same device. The TG3K dataset includes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3, 585 ultrasound images collected from 16 ultrasound videos.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Following the experimental setup described in [53], we com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bine 2, 879 images from TN3K and 3, 585 images from TG3K

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to form the training and validation datasets, while 614 images

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from TN3K and 637 images from DDTI are formed the test

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: set.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3) ISIC Dataset: The ISIC-2018 [56] dataset, provided by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the International Skin Imaging Collaboration (ISIC), is derived

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from a substantial collection of dermoscopy images. It com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: prises 2, 594 images for training and 1, 000 images for testing.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4) ACDC Dataset: The ACDC dataset [57], introduced dur-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing the MICCAI 2017 challenge, includes four classes, (i.e.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: background, right ventricle, left ventricle, and myocardium).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: It comprises imaging scans from 100 patients. Following the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: data partitioning strategy outlined in [4], we split the dataset

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: into 70 scans for training, 10 for validation, and 20 for testing.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5) BCSS Dataset: The Breast Cancer Semantic Segmenta-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion (BCSS) dataset [58] contains 151 pathological images

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of varying sizes. In this study, we utilize an overlap-based

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cropping method to produce a dataset of 3, 888 images, each

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with a resolution of 1024 × 1024 pixels. This choice of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dimension was strategic, aimed at ensuring that each image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1) Implementation Details: All experiments are conducted

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2) Comparison With SAM-Based Semi-Supervised Methods:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this study, we harness the robust segmentation capabilities

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the SAM through distillation learning to enhance the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performance of semi-supervised medical image segmentation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To assess various SAM-based semi-supervised segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: approaches, we compare the proposed model with two other

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SAM-based methods: SemiSAM [22] and CPC-SAM [61].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: It is important to highlight that in CPC-SAM, SAM's outputs

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are treated as the definitive segmentation outcomes, whereas in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: our approach and SemiSAM, the outputs from the UNet model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are regarded as the segmentation maps. Notably, UNet offers

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a significant reduction in inference cost due to its reduced

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: computational demands compared to SAM. Table VIII shows

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a quantitative comparison of SAM-based semi-supervised

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods with 10% and 30%labeled data. It can be observed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that our model consistently outperforms SemiSAM across

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: all datasets, thereby validating its effectiveness. Furthermore,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: our KnowSAM model delivers promising results on several

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: datasets with a lower inference cost, underscoring its ability

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to boost segmentation performance.

layout_dets.text: To further investigate our choice of SAM, we conduct an

layout_dets.text: V. CONCLUSION

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this paper, we have proposed a novel KnowSAM

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: framework for semi-supervised medical image segmentation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: By employing the multi-view co-training paradigm, our model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: enables two subnets to learn from SAM through knowledge

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: distillation, enhancing the generalization capabilities of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: subnets and mitigating the impact of noise in unlabeled data.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Additionally, we present the UGDA strategy to enhance the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model's robustness through the interaction between labeled

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and unlabeled data. This effective strategy also avoids incur-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ring additional costs during inference. Experimental results

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: across various datasets validate the superiority of the proposed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: KnowSAM. It is worth noting that our method can be easily

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: extended to enhance other semi-supervised segmentation tasks.
